Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: ADK sub-agents lose model/instruction due to Pydantic circular ref

Google ADK agents are Pydantic BaseModel subclasses with a parent_agent
back-reference. When serialize_agent() called model_dump() on the parent,
Pydantic's circular reference handling truncated sub-agent serialization
at the BaseAgent boundary, dropping LlmAgent-specific fields (model,
instruction, etc.) from all sub-agents.

Fix: serialize Pydantic v2 models field-by-field using model_fields and
getattr(), letting our own `seen` set handle the circular parent_agent
reference instead of Pydantic's truncation. Also inject _type = class
name so the server-side normalizer can identify orchestrator types
(SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) and select the correct
compilation strategy.

Result: ADK examples with sub_agents now pass (was 16/32 ERROR, now 32/32).

* fix(credentials): inject DataSource by parameter to avoid CGLIB proxy reliance

credentialJdbc() and credentialSchemaInitializer() were calling
credentialDataSource() directly. While Spring's CGLIB proxy on @Configuration
classes returns the same singleton for intra-class bean method calls, making
the injection explicit via @Qualifier parameter is clearer and eliminates any
ambiguity about which DataSource instance each bean receives.

* fix(credentials): fix CredentialEnvSeederTest LIKE wildcard and table-not-exists race

Two issues in cleanUp() @BeforeEach:
- LIKE '_TEST_%' treated leading underscore as a single-char SQL wildcard;
  fixed with ESCAPE '\' so it matches the literal string _TEST_
- DELETE could throw 'no such table' if the DataSourceInitializer had not
  yet run before @BeforeEach fired; wrapped in try/catch to handle gracefully

feat(cli): WIP — full-screen Charmbracelet TUI (#103)

Adds a complete interactive TUI to the agentspan CLI. Running 'agentspan'
with no arguments on a TTY launches the full-screen TUI. All existing
subcommands (agent run, server start, etc.) are unchanged — strictly additive.

─── Architecture ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Package layout:
  cli/tui/ui/           — shared styles, colors, layout helpers (leaf package)
  cli/tui/components/   — StatusBadge, EventLog renderer, KeyMap help overlay
  cli/tui/nav.go        — sidebar navigation (8 items, j/k/enter/tab)
  cli/tui/app.go        — root BubbleTea model, alt-screen, key routing
  cli/tui/views/        — 10 full view implementations
  cli/examples/         — GitHub API fetcher + installer for SDK examples
  cli/internal/serverctl/ — shared server lifecycle (JAR, launch, stop, health)

Dependencies added:
  charm.land/bubbletea/v2, charm.land/lipgloss/v2, charm.land/huh/v2,
  charm.land/bubbles/v2, github.com/charmbracelet/glamour

─── Color palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Lime green #A8FF3E (accent/active) · Green #39D353 (success)
  Dark green #1A7F37 (borders) · Grey #6E7681 (dimmed) · Dark grey #2D333B (bg)

─── Key routing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ↑↓/jk        Navigate sidebar by default on startup
  enter/tab     Open selected view AND focus content panel
  ↑↓ in content Scroll / navigate list
  esc           Return focus to sidebar (views intercept first if they have
                internal state: sub-panes, search mode, confirm dialogs)
  1-8           Jump directly to view (1=Dashboard 2=Agents 3=Executions
                4=Server 5=Skills 6=Credentials 7=Doctor 8=Configure)
  ?             Help overlay · ctrl+c quit (always)

─── Views ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Dashboard
  Inline status bar (server status + URL + agent/execution counts).
  Recent executions table. r→Agents run, enter→detail, R refresh.

Agents (unified hub replacing separate Run/Deploy nav items)
  PaneList    — browsable table + ButtonBar (r run·n new·E examples·D deploy·
                d delete·/search·R refresh). ↓ past list focuses button bar,
                ←→ navigate, enter activates.
  PaneDetail  — full metadata inspect: name/version/type/tags/checksum
  PaneRun     — huh form (agent select + prompt + session) → live SSE stream
  PaneStream  — SSE viewport with follow mode, colour-coded event types:
                thinking(grey)·tool(blue)·result(lime)·handoff(yellow)·error(red)
  PaneDone    — completion state with save/re-run options
  PaneCreate  — huh form to scaffold new agent YAML (agent init equivalent)
  PaneDeploy  — info panel with CLI deploy commands + examples
  PaneExamples — browse 222 examples (111 🐍 Python + 111 📘 TypeScript)
                fetched live from GitHub, multi-select:
                · p/t filter by language · / search by name/tag
                · space toggle · a select/deselect all
                · enter → download → write to cwd → auto pip install agentspan
                          → deploy to server via language-appropriate subprocess
                · Results: FILE | DEPLOY STATUS table per example

Executions
  Paginated history (←→ pages), /search, s stream live, enter→detail.

Execution Status
  Split I/O viewport (JSON input + output, tab to toggle).
  Inline HITL approve/deny when status=WAITING.

Server
  Compact status bar: ● Running · JAR size · PID · CPU% · RAM · Uptime · Threads
  Metrics via ps every 5s. Log viewport fills height with f follow mode.
  s start (real JAR launch via serverctl) · t stop with confirm dialog.
  Live progress during start: JAR check → Java check → health polling.

Credentials
  Tabbed: Credentials | Bindings. ButtonBar (tab·a add·d delete·R refresh).
  huh add forms with full field navigation (all keys forwarded to huh).

Doctor
  Async parallel diagnostics: Java, Python, disk, 11 AI providers, server.
  ✓/✗/– per check. R to re-run. SpinnerTickCmd animates while loading.

Configure
  huh form: Server URL + Auth Key + Auth Secret. ↑↓/tab navigate fields.
  All keys forwarded to huh when form is active.

Skills — stub with CLI usage hints.

─── Layout system ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ContentWidth(termW)  = termW - SidebarWidth - 2
  ContentHeight(termH) = termH - 4  (header + footer + 2 separators)
  RenderLayout pads both panels to termH-4 rows (fills full terminal).
  WindowSizeMsg injected on navigation — views always start at correct size.
  Server log viewport overhead calculated precisely to avoid overflow.

─── Spinner animation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ui.SpinnerTickMsg + ui.SpinnerTickCmd() fires every 100ms.
  All loading views subscribe; spinner only re-fires while loading (no idle).

─── SSE streaming ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Persistent goroutine channels stored in model. nextSSEEvent(ch) Cmd loop
  reads continuously without blocking the BubbleTea update cycle.
  's' on RUNNING execution in Executions view reconnects SSE stream
  via NewAgentsStream() → connectStreamMsg → PaneStream.

─── Server lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  cli/internal/serverctl/ shared between cmd/server.go and TUI:
  EnsureJAR → CheckJava → CheckPortFree → Launch (JVM) → waitHealthy

Add stateful agent mode with task-to-domain routing to prevent cross-instance message mixing

Refine stateful agent: per-tool isolation and fix LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE routing

## Design

Two ways to opt in, same effect:

```python
# Option A — per-tool (only those tools get domain-isolated)
@tool(stateful=True)
def reply_to_user(message: str) -> str: ...

@tool(stateful=True)
def run_task(task_name: str, task_input: str) -> str: ...

agent = Agent(name="chat_repl_agent", tools=[..., reply_to_user, run_task])

# Option B — whole agent (all worker tools get domain-isolated)
@tool
def reply_to_user(message: str) -> str: ...

agent = Agent(name="chat_repl_agent", tools=[..., reply_to_user], stateful=True)
```

Both produce the same outcome: a run_id is generated, matching workers poll
that domain, server routes those tasks there.

## Changes

- `@tool(stateful=True)` decorator param + `ToolDef.stateful` field
- `Agent(stateful=True)` propagates to all worker tools via serializer
- `_has_stateful_tools()` helper checks both agent and tool flags
- Tool registry uses `domain` only for stateful tools (agent OR tool level)
- Server routes only stateful tool names in taskToDomain — fixes LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE
  being routed to the isolated domain where no system task worker polls it
- `ToolConfig.stateful` Java field (no @Builder.Default to avoid Jackson issue)
- Apply `Agent(stateful=True)` to all long-running WMQ examples (75–82)
- Add docs/design/stateful-agents.md

fix(server): harden SQLite busy_timeout + upload test reports on CI failure (#119)

* fix(server): harden SQLite busy_timeout and expose test reports on CI failure

CredentialAwareHttpTaskTest is intermittently failing in CI with an
org.sqlite.SQLiteException at the @BeforeEach storeProvider.set() call.

Two changes:

1. CredentialDataSourceConfig: add connectionInitSql("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 15000")
   for the SQLite path. The test URL uses SQLite's file: URI syntax
   (?mode=memory&cache=shared), where ?-params are SQLite URI parameters
   parsed by the native engine — not JDBC connection properties parsed by
   the xerial driver. That means busy_timeout cannot be set via the URL for
   in-memory databases. connectionInitSql applies it on every new connection
   regardless of URL format, acting as a safety net if HikariCP ever evicts
   and recreates the connection after startup (at which point Conductor's
   one-time initializeSqlite() won't run again and the new connection would
   have busy_timeout=0).

2. CI: upload server test HTML reports as an artifact on failure so the full
   SQLiteException message and stack trace are visible. Gradle's console
   output only shows exception class names; the actual SQLite error code
   (SQLITE_BUSY vs SQLITE_LOCKED vs SQLITE_ERROR) is in the message and is
   needed to confirm the root cause.

* Register termination condition workers in AgentRuntime

Agents with .termination() configured create {agent_name}_termination
SIMPLE tasks that need a client-side worker to evaluate the condition.
The Python SDK registers these automatically; Java now does the same.

Worker logic:
- TextMentionTermination: should_continue = !result.contains(text)
- MaxMessageTermination: should_continue = iteration < maxMessages
- TokenUsageTermination: always continue (token counts not in result)
- AndTermination: stop only when both sub-conditions say stop
- OrTermination: stop when either sub-condition says stop

* Fix WorkerManager to start polling thread for late-registered workers

When workers are registered after startAll() has already been called
(e.g. on the 2nd/3rd Agentspan.run() call via the singleton), no
polling thread was started for the new task type, causing those tasks
to sit SCHEDULED forever.

Fix: if the executor is already running when register() is called,
immediately start a polling thread for the new task name.

* fix(python-sdk): use threads instead of processes for workers on Windows

Windows multiprocessing uses the 'spawn' start method which requires all
objects passed to child processes to be picklable. Conductor workers fail
this requirement because they hold threading.Lock objects and closures
that cannot be pickled.

The fix patches Conductor's task_handler (Windows-only, guarded by
platform.system() == "Windows") to use threading.Thread instead of
multiprocessing.Process for worker execution:

- Avoids all pickling requirements — threads share the parent's memory
- Also patches signal.signal to be a no-op in non-main threads, since
  Conductor's worker targets call it unconditionally (forbidden in threads)

Tool-using examples (02a, 02b, 03, 05, 06, 07 etc.) previously failed
with "cannot pickle '_thread.lock' object" on Windows. All now pass.

Mac/Linux are unaffected — the patch only runs on Windows where fork()
is unavailable.

ci(java-sdk): switch to Sonatype Central Portal API via vanniktech plugin

The OSSRH-shim staging endpoint silently dropped uploads from this
namespace: workflow runs reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL with 12-14s of upload
time, but the artifacts never appeared in any staging API, the
Deployments UI, or repo1.maven.org. Reproduced across rc1, rc2, and 0.1.0.
The shim is the legacy compatibility layer; new namespaces are steered
toward the Portal API ZIP-bundle upload at central.sonatype.com/api/v1
/publisher/upload, which is a different protocol that maven-publish
cannot speak natively.

Replace manual maven-publish + signing + custom promoteToMavenCentral
task with com.vanniktech.maven.publish 0.30.0, which:
- Bundles all artifacts (jar/sources/javadoc/pom/module + signatures)
  into a single ZIP per module.
- POSTs to the Portal API; returns a deployment ID surfaced in the
  Deployments UI.
- Auto-releases to Maven Central when called via
  publishAndReleaseToMavenCentral (configured with
  SonatypeHost.CENTRAL_PORTAL + automaticRelease=true).

Workflow now invokes ./gradlew publishAndReleaseToMavenCentral and
reads credentials/signing material from the plugin's standard env vars
(ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_mavenCentralUsername/Password and
ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_signingInMemoryKey/Id/Password). Existing GitHub
secrets (SONATYPE_USERNAME/PASSWORD, SIGNING_KEY_ID/KEY/PASSWORD) are
unchanged; only the env var names that map them differ.

signAllPublications() is wrapped in a hasProperty guard so
publishToMavenLocal continues to work without signing material on
developer machines.

for native agents, or `framework`+`rawConfig` for framework-backed agents (which

null model and fail compilation at ModelParser.parse().

agent.getFramework() is non-null (except "skill", which currently includes a
synthetic model to stay on the native path).

* fix(java): JSON-serialize Map/List values when LLM passes them for String-typed @Tool params

When the LLM emits a JSON object or array for a @Tool parameter declared as
String, LangChain4jAgent.coerce() was calling value.toString() — which on Java
Maps returns `{key=value}` (Java's Map.toString format), not JSON. This broke
tools that parse the string argument back as JSON.

Concrete example: in ExampleLc4j25AdvancedOrchestration, calculate_metric's
`String values` parameter received `{"initial_value": 200, "years": 6}` from
the LLM. Java received it as a Map, called toString, and the example's parser
saw `{initial_value=200, years=6}` and rejected it as not-JSON.

Fix: when targetType is String and value is Map/List, run it through
JsonMapper instead of Object.toString(). Restores Python's behaviour

stream.approve() was 500ing under Strategy.HANDOFF because two issues compounded:

event has no execution id, so misuse fails loud rather than silently falling
back to the wrong target.

behavior that AgentHumanTask emits the owning execution id on WAITING events.

first per repo convention. Also fixes a latent bug in send(message) which
previously built a body but never sent it.

* fix: register handoff_check worker for SWARM parents without explicit handoffs

Server always generates {parent}_handoff_check for SWARM workflows, but SDK
only registered the worker when agent.handoffs was truthy. This caused SWARM
loops (like coder↔qa) to deadlock when the parent had no explicit handoffs
(only children had OnTextMention handoffs).

strategy === "swarm") unlike the Python bug, but had no tests proving it.

* feat(sdk): add _resolve_worker_domain + use worker_domain at 4 sites

Required for Mode A idempotency-replay handling: when the server
returns an existing execution for an idempotency_key, workers must
register under the workflow's original taskToDomain, not the freshly
generated run_id. This was assumed by the design spec but was actually
uncommitted user work on coding_agent — pulling it forward here.

Updates the 4 start/stream call sites to compute worker_domain via
_resolve_worker_domain(execution_id, run_id) and use it for
_prepare_workers, _register_and_start_skill_workers, and the
LocalLivenessCheck registered-pair query.

* fix(sdk): re-register stateful workers when polling domain changes

A stateful agent re-run with the same task names but a different
``run_id`` (e.g., a fresh execution that isn't an idempotency replay)
needs ``WorkerManager.start()`` to register the new ``(task_name,
domain)`` pairs. The previous ``elif new_workers:`` branch only fired
when the *task-name set* changed; identical names under a different
domain were silently skipped, leaving the new domain unpolled.

Convert to ``else:`` at all four sites (sync/async ``run`` and
``start``, plus the framework and graph paths). ``WorkerManager`` is
domain-aware and only spawns missing pairs, so this remains safe under
concurrent re-runs and avoids the fork() deadlock window of a full
stop/restart cycle.

Adds test_prepare_workers_starts_worker_manager_when_only_domain_changes
to lock the contract: start() is called once even when the task names
have already been registered, as long as the domain differs.

* fix(server): preserve tool output in conversation history

The previous compactToolHistory implementation truncated any tool result
older than the 6 most recent to 500 chars (with '...[truncated]'). That
caused the agent to lose context — a 5KB glob_find result kept only ~500
chars of file names, so on the next turn the agent re-issued the same
glob_find with a different filter, then re-read the same files. Observed
in workflow 637d179b-e0b5-4efd-a33f-2b2811ccbc01 where iter 14's
glob_find result was clipped to '...AgentspanAIMod...[truncated]' and
the agent kept reissuing nearly-identical queries trying to see more.

Removed:
  * Mid-conversation truncation of older tool results
  * contextbook_read 'keep only latest per section' dedup (relied on
    truncation; now that we keep full results, dedup is unnecessary)
  * truncateToolResult helper and TOOL_RESULT_TRUNCATE_LENGTH /
    RECENT_TOOL_RESULTS_TO_KEEP constants — no longer used

Kept:
  * Write-only tool collapsing — contextbook_write / contextbook_summary
    produce 'wrote N chars' confirmations that add no downstream value
    and are emitted by the agent itself (can't lose information)

Token-budget pressure flows through condenseIfNeeded, which drops ENTIRE
old messages — cleaner than partial truncation since the agent either
has full context for a message or doesn't see it at all.

fix(server): restore AgentConfig.synthesize + final-LLM elision (#242)

The PAC/PAE commit (acbde7d8) accidentally removed:

  * ``AgentConfig.synthesize`` (the field that gated the final-LLM
    synthesis step on HANDOFF / ROUTER / SWARM strategies, added by
    PR #189);
  * The ``if (config.isSynthesize()) tasks.add(finalLlm);`` guards at
    the three call sites in MultiAgentCompiler.

Result: ``synthesize=false`` was silently ignored — the SDKs serialized
the flag but the server's Jackson dropped it on deserialise (no field),
and the workflow always emitted the ``_final`` LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE task.
The Java ``Suite16Synthesize`` e2e suite caught this once it started
running in CI (3 / 4 tests failing).

Restore in three pieces:

* ``AgentConfig.synthesize`` — modelled as nullable ``Boolean`` (not
  primitive + Builder.Default) so ``@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)`` keeps the
  field out of serialized output when callers leave it unset. The Java
  SDK's ``Suite16Synthesize`` test asserts the agentDef metadata MUST
  NOT contain ``synthesize`` when the flag is at its default — a
  primitive-with-default would always have emitted it as ``true`` and
  failed that contract.
* ``AgentConfig.isSynthesize()`` — manual getter treating ``null`` as
  ``true`` so existing compiler call sites read the right default.
* ``MultiAgentCompiler`` — restore the ``isSynthesize()`` guards at all
  three sites (handoff at ~390, router at ~981, swarm at ~1271) so
  ``synthesize=false`` skips the ``_final`` task and routes
  ``${workflow.variables.conversation}`` directly to the workflow's
  ``result`` output instead of the missing ``_final.output.result``.

* ``./gradlew test`` (server) → 570 / 570 pass.
* ``./gradlew test -Pe2e --tests Suite16Synthesize`` (sdk/java) →
  4 / 4 pass against PR #238 server.

fix(py-e2e): scope test_local_timeout assertion to the sleep task (#245)

The test prompts the agent with ``time.sleep(30); print("done")`` and
asserts the 3-second executor timeout kills it before ``print`` runs.
It then iterates **every** ``execute_code`` task in the workflow and
fails if any has ``"done"`` in stdout.

With ``max_turns=2`` the agent has a second LLM turn after the first
task times out — and gpt-4o-mini's usual response is to "fix" the
problem by re-running just ``print("done")`` without the sleep. That
follow-up task legitimately completes with ``stdout="done\n"``, and
the loop fails on it:

    assert 'done' not in 'done\n'

even though the original sleep call **did** time out as the test was
actually trying to verify.

Scope the assertion to tasks whose input code contains ``sleep`` —
the contract is "the sleeping code timed out", not "no code ever
completed across the whole run". Symmetric scoping on the
"timeout-error-appeared" assertion. Also surface a clearer error
when the LLM never invoked the tool with the sleep snippet at all.

* fix(java-sdk): emit worker_ref tool shape + keep langchain4j at runtime

Two related bugs that together broke every tool-using OpenAI Agents or
Google ADK example: the LLM saw paramless tools (or no tools at all),
called them with empty inputData, and the worker threw NPE — the
example then thrashed with up to 120 retries.

1) AgentConfigSerializer (openai / google_adk branch) was emitting the
   standard `{name, description, inputSchema, toolType}` tool shape.
   The server's OpenAINormalizer and GoogleADKNormalizer only read
   `_worker_ref` + `description` + `parameters` — Python's
   frameworks/serializer.py does the same. Without a `_worker_ref`, the
   normalizers dropped the schema and the model received tools with no
   parameter information.

2) examples/build.gradle had `dev.langchain4j:langchain4j` as
   compileOnly. The @Tool / @P annotations are RUNTIME-retained, but
   when their declaring class isn't on the runtime classpath the JVM
   silently strips them from getAnnotations(). Reflection then sees no
   annotations and returns an empty tool list — agent.getTools() is
   empty, so the rawConfig has no `tools` field, so the model sees no
   tools at all. Pinning langchain4j as runtimeOnly too matches what
   PR #223's examples/build.gradle already did for LangChain4j.

Verified end-to-end:
- ExampleOpenAi02FunctionTools: 120 calls / 45441 tokens (FAILED) →
  3 calls / 717 tokens (COMPLETED) with correct weather + population +
  sqrt answers.
- ExampleAdk02FunctionTools: 0 tool calls (model said it has no
  real-time data) → 4 tool calls / 1232 tokens (COMPLETED) with
  Tokyo weather, °F conversion, and JST timezone.

* fix(java): emit AgentTool marker shape in framework serializer

When a tool with toolType="agent_tool" appears on an OpenAI/ADK framework
agent, the serializer was emitting the generic worker_ref shape
(_worker_ref/description/parameters), which made the server compile it as
a regular tool task waiting for an SDK worker. The Java SDK has no worker
for the sub-agent's name, so the workflow stalled until the AgentHandle's
10-minute timeout.

Mirror Python's _try_extract_agent_tool (frameworks/serializer.py:272) —
when toolType=="agent_tool" and the tool has an agentRef, emit:

    {"_type": "AgentTool", "name", "description", "agent": <serialized child>}

The framework normalizer then compiles this as a SUB_WORKFLOW task that
runs the child agent inline, returning its output as the tool result.

complete end-to-end:

- ADK 33 → workflow a5be2546-..., 4 tool calls, 1427 tokens

* fix(java-adk-bridge): bug-bounty pass — cycles, leaks, plan-routing, coerce

Adversarial review surfaced ten real bugs in the ADK bridge / dispatcher /
runtime. This commit closes the high- and medium-severity ones; the
remaining issues are P2 polish documented inline.

## P0 — Infinite recursion on subAgents / AgentTool cycles

AdkBridge.toAgentspan and buildRawConfig recursed on subAgents and
AgentTool.getAgent() without a visited-set. A self-loop or A->B->A graph
would StackOverflow. Both recursion paths now thread an
IdentityHashMap<BaseAgent, Boolean> visited; second visit throws
IllegalArgumentException naming the offending agent.

## P0 — BaseToolset.close() never called

McpToolset and other AutoCloseable toolsets leaked the underlying
process / socket every time the bridge expanded them. addToolMap now
wraps expansion in try/finally that always calls close(). Expansion
failures also escalated from log.warn to log.error since the user
silently loses tools otherwise.

## P0 — Anemic coerce — replaced with ToolRegistry.coerceArgument

The bridge's local coerce() handled only String + primitives + Boolean.
List<X>, Map<String, Object>, arrays, enums, java.time.* (LocalDate,
Instant, etc.), Optional<T> all fell through to Method.invoke and threw
"argument type mismatch". The fix for @Tool in #236 (commit 420d9202)
addressed this for native Agentspan tools but never propagated to
AdkBridge. Promoted ToolRegistry.coerce(value, type, genericType) to a
public coerceArgument(...) helper; AdkBridge.buildArgs now delegates to
it. Generic types are now passed through so List<Double> is correctly
constructed from JSON arrays.

## P0 — paramName silently returned arg0/arg1 without -parameters

When a method has no -parameters compiler flag and no @Schema(name=),
Parameter.getName() returns "arg0", "arg1". The LLM saw these in the
function schema. Now paramName logs a warn-once-per-method instructing
the user to compile with -parameters or use @Schema(name=...).

## P1 — InvocationTargetException double-wrap

ADK FunctionTool invoke caught Exception and rethrew as
RuntimeException, hiding the real cause two layers deep behind
InvocationTargetException. Now explicitly unwraps ITE.getCause() and
rethrows RuntimeExceptions directly; only wraps checked exceptions.
The error message now includes a hint about -parameters when the cause
is an IllegalArgumentException (likely an arg-type mismatch).

## P1 — Agentspan.plan(LlmAgent) ignored framework routing

Same bug we fixed for deploy() last commit, just on /api/agent/compile.
plan(adkAgent) failed with "TaskDef name cannot be null" because the
framework rawConfig was being shipped under {agentConfig:...} rather
than {framework, rawConfig}. HttpApi.compileAgent gained a
framework-aware overload; AgentRuntime.plan dispatches like startAsync
and deploy. Verified: plan() now returns a workflowDef.

## P1 — deploy() / serve() with no agents

deploy() returned an empty list silently (no work done). serve() called
Thread.currentThread().join() with zero workers registered — it would
block forever waiting for tasks no one would ever post. Both throw
IllegalArgumentException now with a clear message.

## P1 — coerceAgents swallowed the failing index

deploy(a, null, c) threw "agent is null" with no clue which slot was
bad. Now wraps with "agents[1]: agent is null".

## P2 — isInstanceOf recurses through superinterface chains

Walked superclass chain plus direct interfaces only. Doesn't matter for
ADK BaseAgent (a class) today but breaks for any future interface-typed
framework target (Vercel AI, etc.). Replaced with a single recursive
matchesType() that walks all supertypes.

## P2 — Dead code cleanup

Removed THINKING_CONFIG_CLASS / GENERATE_CONTENT_CONFIG_CLASS vestigial
static fields. ThinkingConfig and GenerateContentConfig are now used
directly in buildRawConfig — the IDE-keepalive hack is no longer needed.

## Verified

- 5/5 edge-case probes pass: cycle detection no false-positives;
  deploy()/serve() empty throw IAE; deploy(a, null, c) reports
  agents[1]; plan(LlmAgent) returns workflowDef.
- 9/9 representative ADK example smoke battery COMPLETED with zero
  AdkBridge warning logs.

## Not fixed in this pass (documented, lower severity)

- Instruction.Provider with null context silently returns null (server
  prompt loss is logged but not fatal). Improving this requires either
  passing a synthetic context or hard-failing — needs design call.
- Cross-classloader ClassCastException in OSGi / fat-jar setups (rare).
- Callback hook tasks not yet compiled server-side; Python has the same
  gap. Tracked separately.

* feat(java-adk): deploy/serve example + Agentspan guardrails on ADK agents

## Two new examples

**Example37DeployAndServe.java** — full deploy + serve + run round-trip
in a single JVM. Demonstrates each Agentspan entry point with a native
ADK LlmAgent and no bridge calls in user code:

  1. `Agentspan.deploy(agent)`  — register on the server (CI/CD)
  2. `Agentspan.serve(agent)`   — register local workers + poll
                                  (daemon thread for the demo)
  3. `Agentspan.start(agent, prompt)` — trigger an execution

The serve thread picks up the `lookup_user` tool task; the start call
returns an AgentHandle that resolves to a COMPLETED AgentResult.

**Example38AgentspanGuardrails.java** — attaches Agentspan's
server-compiled guardrail mechanism to a native ADK agent for the
first time. ADK has no built-in guardrail abstraction (its safety
story is beforeModelCallback short-circuits, which the server doesn't
yet compile into hook tasks). Agentspan's `GuardrailDef` compiles
into a Conductor task inside the agent's DoWhile loop and can `pass`,
`fail`, or `fix` the LLM's output.

The example registers a PII-redaction guardrail with `OnFail.FIX`,
runs an LLM that produces `alice@example.com` / `555-867-5309`, and
the final output shown to the user is `[EMAIL REDACTED]` /
`[PHONE REDACTED]` — proving the server-side rewrite path.

## Three fixes to make Example38 actually fire

1. `AgentConfigSerializer` framework path (openai / google_adk)
   silently dropped `agent.getGuardrails()` — the wire payload had no
   guardrails field, so the server never saw any. Now emits
   `serializeGuardrail(...)` entries in the framework map just like
   the native Agentspan path does.

2. `GoogleADKNormalizer` did not extract `guardrails` from the raw
   config — even with the SDK fix, the server never built any
   GuardrailConfig. Added `addGuardrails` / `normalizeGuardrail`
   helpers mirroring OpenAINormalizer's existing implementation.

3. The normalizer's worker-ref lookup omitted the `taskName` field
   the SDK actually emits (Python convention:
   `<agentName>_output_guardrail`). It only checked `_worker_ref` and
   nested forms, so the compiled task name defaulted to the
   guardrail's own name (`pii_redaction`) — which didn't match the
   worker the SDK had registered (`contact_directory_output_guardrail`).
   The Conductor task sat SCHEDULED forever. Now reads `taskName` first.

## API touch-ups

- `Agent.Builder.guardrails(GuardrailDef...)` varargs overload added
  for fluent usage; the existing `List<GuardrailDef>` form is
  preserved.
- `AdkBridge.agentBuilder(BaseAgent)` exposes the populated
  `Agent.Builder` so users can attach Agentspan-only features
  (guardrails, gate, termination, callbacks) on top of a native ADK
  agent without breaking the drop-in pattern:

    Agent decorated = AdkBridge.agentBuilder(adk)
        .guardrails(piiGuard)
        .build();
    Agentspan.run(decorated, prompt);

* feat(java-langchain-langgraph): same shape as ADK — bridges + bug-bounty parity

Brings LangChain4j and LangGraph4j integrations to the same production
shape we landed for ADK: bridges in the core SDK, bug-bounty fixes
applied to the shared LangChain4jAgent tool extractor, and
guardrail-decoration via `agentBuilder(...)` instead of just
`toAgentspan(...)`.

## Bridges moved into the core SDK

- `examples/.../langchain/LangChainBridge.java`
  → `src/main/java/ai/agentspan/frameworks/LangChainBridge.java`
- `examples/.../langgraph/LangGraphBridge.java`
  → `src/main/java/ai/agentspan/frameworks/LangGraphBridge.java`

`langchain4j-open-ai`, `langgraph4j-core`, and
`langgraph4j-agent-executor` are now `compileOnly` deps of the SDK.
The bridge classes only link at runtime when the user actually passes
a `ChatModel` or builds an `AgentExecutor`, so users who don't use
these frameworks pay nothing.

All 27 LangChain and 12 LangGraph example files had their imports
updated to point at the new `ai.agentspan.frameworks.*` location.

## Same bug-bounty fixes that landed for ADK

`LangChain4jAgent` is the load-bearing tool extractor used by both
LangChainBridge and LangGraphBridge. It had the same three bugs that
AdkBridge had:

1. **Anemic `coerce()`** — handled only String + primitives + Boolean.
   `List<X>` / `Map` / arrays / enums / `java.time.*` / `Optional<T>`
   all fell through to `Method.invoke` and threw `IllegalArgumentException:
   argument type mismatch`. Now delegates to
   `ToolRegistry.coerceArgument(value, type, genericType)` with the
   generic parameterized type, matching the @Tool fix in #236.

2. **Param-name silently returned `arg0`** without `-parameters`. Now
   logs a warn-once-per-method telling the user to compile with
   `-parameters` or use `@P("...")`.

3. **`InvocationTargetException` double-wrap** buried the user's real
   exception two layers deep. Now unwraps `ITE.getCause()` and
   rethrows `RuntimeException`s directly; wraps checked exceptions
   with a hint about `-parameters`.

## `agentBuilder(...)` for guardrail decoration

Mirroring `AdkBridge.agentBuilder`, both bridges expose a `.agentBuilder(...)`
that returns the populated `Agent.Builder` so users can attach
Agentspan-only features (guardrails, gate, termination, callbacks) on
top of a native LangChain4j or LangGraph4j agent:

```java
Agent guarded = LangChainBridge.agentBuilder("name", model, "prompt", new MyTools())
    .guardrails(piiGuard)
    .build();
Agentspan.run(guarded, "...");
```

The `toAgentspan(...)` methods stay as a shortcut for the common
no-decoration case.

## New example: Example26AgentspanGuardrails (LangChain)

Mirrors `adk.Example38AgentspanGuardrails`. Builds a native
`OpenAiChatModel`, attaches a PII-redaction `GuardrailDef` with
`OnFail.FIX`, runs an LLM that emits raw `alice@example.com` /
`555-867-5309`, and the user sees `[EMAIL REDACTED]` / `[PHONE REDACTED]`.

## Why no native CompiledGraph drop-in for LangGraph

Investigated and deferred. LangGraph4j's `StateGraph` /
`CompiledGraph` has no native "agent name" attribute — users would
still have to pass a name as a separate argument, which loses the
clean drop-in story. The current
`LangGraphBridge.toAgentspan(name, model, prompt, tools)` is already
a single-line invocation; reflection into the compiled graph to
extract model + tools adds risk without meaningfully shortening the
user's code.

## Why no server-side LangChain/LangGraph normalizer fixes

The bridges call `LangChain4jAgent.from(...)` which builds an
Agentspan Agent **without** `.framework(...)` set. So LangChain and
LangGraph examples already route through the native Agentspan compile
path (which fully supports guardrails); the `LangChainNormalizer` and
`LangGraphNormalizer` are dormant for the current examples. The
guardrail/taskName fix we made for `GoogleADKNormalizer` doesn't apply
here because that code path isn't exercised.

* feat(java-langchain-langgraph): true drop-in — no bridge calls in user code

User feedback: the LangChainBridge.toAgentspan(...) call in every
LangChain/LangGraph example didn't match the clean ADK pattern of
"native object goes straight to Agentspan.run". This commit closes
that gap with native-type overloads on every Agentspan entry point.

## New drop-in shapes

LangChain4j idiom — ChatModel + @Tool POJOs:
```java
ChatModel model = OpenAiChatModel.builder()...build();
Agentspan.run(model, "user prompt");                     // no tools
Agentspan.run(model, "user prompt", new MyTools());      // with tools
Agentspan.deploy(model, new MyTools());                  // deploy
Agentspan.serve(model, new MyTools());                   // serve
```

LangGraph4j idiom — AgentExecutor.Builder + tool POJOs:
```java
MyTools tools = new MyTools();
AgentExecutor.Builder agent = AgentExecutor.builder().chatModel(model);
agent.toolsFromObject(tools);
Agentspan.run(agent, "user prompt", tools);
```

Both forms support run / runAsync / start / stream / deploy / serve.
The Builder variant reflectively reads `chatModel` and `systemMessage`
from package-private fields, validates the LangGraph4j config builds
successfully, then routes the same path the bridge always used. Tool
POJOs travel separately because the LangGraph4j Builder doesn't
preserve references to the original objects after toolsFromObject().

## Overload-resolution detail (subtle)

Without explicit 2-arg overloads, `Agentspan.run(model, "prompt")`
would lose method resolution against the fixed-arity
`run(Object, String)` since Java prefers non-varargs over varargs
when both are applicable. Added explicit 2-arg variants
(`run(ChatModel, String)`, `run(AgentExecutor.Builder, String)`,
plus matching runAsync/start/stream/deploy/serve) so the drop-in
dispatches even when no tools are passed.

* docs(java-langchain-langgraph): apiKey is server-handled — drop misleading env-var

User feedback: every LangChain / LangGraph example read OPENAI_API_KEY
from env and stamped it onto OpenAiChatModel.builder().apiKey(...) —
which is dishonest. Agentspan **never uses** the client-side apiKey:
the actual LLM call happens server-side using credentials registered
with the Agentspan server.

Confirmed experimentally: passing a deliberately bogus apiKey
"THIS_KEY_IS_BOGUS_SERVER_HANDLES_CREDENTIALS" returns COMPLETED
because the client never touches it.

## Fix

Replaced the env-var pattern in 39 files with a clear constant
placeholder + a two-line comment explaining the server handles
credentials:

```java
// apiKey is required by LangChain4j's builder but unused — Agentspan
// runs the LLM call on the server with server-registered credentials.
ChatModel model = OpenAiChatModel.builder()
        .apiKey("agentspan-server-handles-credentials")
        .modelName("gpt-4o-mini")
        .build();
```

Also updated Javadoc "Requirements" blocks in 24 files: dropped the
client-side OPENAI_API_KEY claim, kept "Agentspan server with OpenAI
credentials configured server-side."

grep across both folders returns zero OPENAI_API_KEY references for

ExampleCredentials.java are unrelated (WEATHER_API_KEY for a

feat: Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE — PAC/PAE compile-and-execute for LLM plans (#238)

* feat: Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE — PAC/PAE compile-and-execute for LLM plans

Introduces Plan-And-Compile / Plan-And-Execute (PAC/PAE) for agents:
a planner LLM produces a structured JSON plan (DAG of operations), the
plan is compiled to a deterministic Conductor sub-workflow, and the
sub-workflow runs without further LLM involvement except where the
plan explicitly calls a 'generate' op. Optional fallback agent runs
agentically when the plan can't compile or fails at execution.

  * **PlanAndCompileTask / PlanAndCompileTaskConfig** — new SIMPLE task
    that runs the planner, extracts the JSON plan from its output (with
    markdown_plan + planSource fallback), and compiles it into a
    sub-workflow definition.
  * **Custom Join task override** — dev.agentspan.runtime.tasks.Join
    replaces Conductor's built-in JOIN to produce compact output
    (only _state_updates + state) for the parallel FORK_JOIN
    aggregator that PAC/PAE uses for plan-step validations.  AgentRuntime
    @ComponentScan excludes Conductor's Join class so our @Component
    is the sole "JOIN" bean.
  * **MultiAgentCompiler** — dispatch on Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE; named
    planner / fallback slots replace the legacy agents=[planner, fallback]
    indexing.
  * **JavaScriptBuilder** — synth_output_script generator and a new
    knownToolNames param on enrichToolsScript so the compiled JS can
    reject hallucinated tool names with a clear error rather than
    silently dispatching to nothing.
  * **AgentConfig** — fallbackMaxTurns, planSource, planner (AgentConfig),
    fallback (AgentConfig) fields.
  * **WorkflowTaskUtils** — helpers for building INLINE / SUB_WORKFLOW
    tasks consistently from the compiler.
  * **PrefillToolCallConfig** — server-side type for tool calls executed
    before the first LLM turn.
  * **GraalVM polyglot test deps** — needed for SynthOutputScriptTest
    and EnrichToolsScriptTest which evaluate the generated JS in-process.
  * Tests: PlanAndCompileTaskTest, SynthOutputScriptTest,
    EnrichToolsScriptTest, ModelContextWindowsTest.

  * **Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE** — new enum value across all three SDKs.
  * **plans.py / PlanExecute / plan_execute()** — typed plan-builder
    helpers (Python) so callers don't hand-roll the JSON plan shape.

* fix(server): bump SQLite credential pool from 1 to 8

The credential pool was capped at maximumPoolSize=1 on SQLite because of a
conservative 'no concurrent writers' assumption. In practice the JDBC URL
enables WAL mode (?journal_mode=WAL), which supports concurrent readers
and a single writer — exactly the workload AgentspanAIModelProvider
generates: per-LLM-call credential resolution is read-only and dominates;
credential writes only happen via the /credentials POST endpoint and
busy_timeout=15000 absorbs the rare contention.

Under PAC/PAE workloads (planner LLM call + N parallel generate-block LLM
calls + optional fallback) the single connection serializes all reads,
producing HikariCP timeouts under load:

  HTTP 500 - 'credential-pool - Connection is not available, request
   timed out after 30000ms (total=1, active=1, idle=0, waiting=39)'

PR #238's typescript-e2e showed ~16 of 18 failures with this error.
A pool of 8 (matching the Postgres pool) eliminates the serialization
without changing concurrency semantics — SQLite still serializes writes
at the file level, just not reads.

* fix(server): guard collectSimpleTaskNamesFromTasks against PAC/PAE runtime-expression workflowDefinition

PlanAndCompileTask builds the compiled SUB_WORKFLOW lazily at runtime
and the parent workflow refers to it via a string-template expression:

  subParams.setWorkflowDefinition("${" + compileRef + ".output.workflowDef}")

(MultiAgentCompiler.java line 2467). At runtime Conductor resolves the
expression to the actual WorkflowDef. At compile time, however,
AgentService.start() calls collectSimpleTaskNames to enumerate worker
names for the SDK, and that recursive walker did:

  if (task.getSubWorkflowParam() != null
          && task.getSubWorkflowParam().getWorkflowDef() != null) {
      ...
  }

— blindly invoking SubWorkflowParams.getWorkflowDef() which casts the
underlying Object to WorkflowDef. With the PAC/PAE template String in
the slot, the cast threw:

  HTTP 500
  'class java.lang.String cannot be cast to class
   com.netflix.conductor.common.metadata.workflow.WorkflowDef'

(test_suite20 PAC/PAE tests).

Fix: use the same instanceof-pattern guard already employed in
AgentCompiler.deduplicateRefs (line 2064-2068). If the slot holds a
WorkflowDef, recurse into its tasks; if it holds a String (runtime
expression), there are no SIMPLE task names to collect statically and we
skip — PlanAndCompileTask emits the inner SIMPLE names through
requiredWorkers at runtime.

* fix(compiler): three TS-e2e regressions — LLM task name, ctx_inject separator, termination short-circuit

Three independent bugs in the agent compiler that each caused a different
TS-e2e suite to fail on PR #238 but pass on main. Confirmed locally via
direct API compile/start against both servers.

1. ``WorkflowTaskUtils.ensureTaskName`` only set the LLM task's TaskDef
   name to ``llm_chat_complete`` when it was empty — but every compile
   site explicitly sets it to ``LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE`` (matching the task
   type). Conductor then misses the registered TaskDef, falls back to
   default tool-routing config, and gpt-4o-mini stops emitting tool
   calls. Always normalize to lowercase.

2. ``contextInjectionScript`` returned an empty string when no state /
   signals existed, but the caller joined it to the prompt with a
   literal ``\n\n``. Empty prefix → ``\n\n<prompt>`` lands at the LLM,
   which at temperature 0 shifts model behavior (e.g. STOP instead of
   TOOL_CALLS). Move the separator into the script (trailing ``\n\n``
   when non-empty, empty otherwise) and drop the literal from the
   message template.

3. The loop's ``termination`` clause was wrapped in
   ``($.llm['finishReason'] == 'TOOL_CALLS' || ...should_continue)``
   so the loop kept iterating past MaxMessage / TokenUsage caps on
   every tool-call turn. The bypass was intended to skip text-based
   terminations on tool-call turns, but text_mention / stop_message
   already return should_continue=true on empty results — the OR
   wasn't needed for them and silently broke count-based terminations.

   most commonly after HITL approve/reject. Captured SSE events are
   preserved on the returned AgentResult; status is the server's view.

2) **Test** — Suite12HandoffApprove:
   - maxTurns(1) on the parent + maxTurns(2) on dba bound the loop: one
     LLM call routes the handoff and the parent's loop exits. (Parent

     `test_hitl_approve_path` pattern.

agent's LLM-loop recovery can serve those semantics. PAC used to log a
warning and continue, leaving users with a silently-degraded pipeline
that ends on the first guardrail trip instead of retrying.

offending tool:guardrail pairs and pointing at the two valid fixes:
configure a fallback agent, or set on_fail=raise. Invert the existing
"compilesButWarns" test, add positive cases for the "with fallback" and
"on_fail=raise without fallback" paths, and update the failure-modes

* fix(pac): reject parallel-step Ref feeding scalar-arg consumers at compile time

A parallel step's output is the FORK_JOIN aggregator array, not a single
result. Previously PAC validated Ref existence, depends_on declaration,
and no-self-Ref — but never compared producer-parallel-vs-consumer-shape.
A user wiring Ref("write_all") into args={"document": Ref("write_all")}
where the tool's inputSchema declared `type: "object"` would compile
fine and explode 5 task-references deep at run time.

Add a compile-time check in PAC's Pass-2 validation: when a top-level
args.<argName> is a direct $ref to a parallel step, look up the consumer
tool's inputSchema.properties.<argName>.type. Reject if it's anything
other than "array" (or missing — we can't type-check what we can't see).
Nested Refs are out of scope: those are LLM-composed values where the
type model is the containing object, not the Ref's target.

Tests cover the failing case (scalar consumer + parallel producer →
compile error), the matching case (array consumer + parallel producer →
ok), and the negative-control (sequential producer + scalar consumer →
ok). Diagnostic message names the offending step + arg + the two valid
fixes.

* docs(plan-execute): add 109 plan-execute-replan loop example + tests

PAE is single-shot — plan-once, execute-once, fallback-once on hard
failure. The first-principles review surfaced this as the largest gap
for non-trivial autonomous tasks: there's no native primitive for
"run, look at output, decide done/replan, iterate." This example
demonstrates the user-space composition pattern that fills that gap
today:

  iteration N:
    1. compile + execute plan_N via PAE (deterministic inner)
    2. read artifacts the run produced (file IO sidesteps the
       per-step-output-not-surfaced-on-AgentResult limitation)
    3. decider() → done | replan
    4. if replan, build plan_{N+1} with the prior iteration's
       measurements baked into per-op generate.instructions
    5. loop, bounded by max_iterations

Task domain: research report with a word-count quality gate. Each
iteration writes N parallel sections (generate ops), assembles them,
and exits the loop once the threshold is met. The replanner feeds the
current word count + target into the LLM's instructions so the next
iteration's content is substantially longer — not just a re-roll of
the same brief.

Decider is rule-based (deterministic, cheap) per CLAUDE.md's "no LLM
for validation" rule. The example notes how to swap in an LLM decider
for subjective-quality cases; the loop shape doesn't change.

Tests pin the pure-function invariants (plan shape, deficit-baking,
decider boundary conditions, target growth with deficit). Verified
test validity per CLAUDE.md by temporarily breaking decide() and
confirming exactly the threshold-met test fails — then restored.

Adds a Plan → execute → replan section to docs/concepts/plan-execute.md
pointing at this example as the canonical answer to "what about
iterative refinement?"

* docs(plan-execute): add 110 adaptive plan-execute-replan goal-seeking loop

Example 109 demonstrated the *shape* of an outer replan loop. Example 110
shows the *adaptive* variant where each iteration's plan is genuinely
informed by what the previous iteration's execution discovered.

The loop:
  iteration N:
    1. plan = build_plan(N, prior_failures)
         ↳ if N > 0: instructions list each prior candidate + which
           specific constraints it failed.
    2. execute plan: K parallel write_candidate generate ops feeding a
       deterministic verify_candidates step.
    3. read verdict.json from disk
    4. if any candidate cleared every constraint → DONE
    5. else carry the per-candidate failure breakdown into N+1

Task domain: write a sentence satisfying first-word / last-word /
keyword-set / exact-word-count constraints. LLMs excel at sentence
generation so the loop converges in 1-3 iterations on default-mini
models — but exact word counts are pathological enough to typically
force one replan, which is what makes the loop visible. Live-tested:
gpt-4o-mini iter 0 produced 20+21 word candidates, replan baked the
deficit into the next prompt, iter 1 produced a 25-word winner.

Per-position style hints differentiate the K parallel proposers
because uniform prompts make them emit identical answers (observed
empirically across gpt-4o-mini and claude-haiku). Tested with 10 unit
tests pinning the pure logic — primality of the loop logic, prompt
feedback construction, plan shape, per-position differentiation,
end-to-end verifier integration via tmp_path. Test validity proven
per CLAUDE.md by deliberately breaking the wrong_first_word branch
and watching exactly the multi-failure test fail; restored.

Also exercises the F3 finding from the design review (output_schema
is documentation, not validation): the LLM sometimes emits the value
field as a JSON number instead of a string. write_candidate accepts
``value`` untyped and coerces to str — a teaching example of the
tool-author burden until a JSON-Schema validator lands in PAC.

* fix(ts-e2e): cap vitest forks at 2 to prevent Conductor overload

GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest now uses 4-core runners. Vitest defaults to
maxForks = cpuCount - 1 = 3, so suites 17, 18, and 20 all start their
20–27 LLM-backed workflows simultaneously (~50+ workflows competing for
the same Conductor + LLM quota). Workers stop-and-restart on every
runtime.start() call (startPolling calls stopPolling first), creating
gaps that let tasks pile up. The combined overload causes every retry
and multi-agent workflow to hit the 300 s polling budget.

Fix: explicitly set maxForks: 2. At most two heavy suites overlap at once
instead of three, staying within Conductor capacity. Two-way parallelism
keeps the wall-clock time at the ~15 min target without sequential
execution.

  runner rebuild so workers poll the correct per-execution queue (not the default)

Three concerns from the OCG branch code review:

   server-side agents are written at @PostConstruct and don't change at
   runtime, so the per-request fetch was wasted work. Added a volatile
   List<AutoExposedEntry> cache with double-checked locking: successes
   cached for the lifetime of the bean, transient DAO failures left
   uncached so the next compile retries (matches the existing "merge is a

refactor(compiler): source auto-exposed tools from RegisteredAgent beans, not a DAO scan

AutoExposedToolsMerger previously discovered auto-exposed sub-agents by
scanning the metadata store for WorkflowDefs stamped with a metadata
marker, caching the result forever. The data it was reading back came
from the same Spring context: the registrar wrote RegisteredAgent beans
into the DAO, then the merger scanned them back out. That round-trip is
what created the bootstrap-ordering trap (a compile during @PostConstruct
froze an empty cache for the bean's lifetime, silently hiding every
registered agent — see 879851f8) plus the lazy cache, the
transient-failure retry carve-out, and the untyped metadata parsing.

Now the merger builds its entries from List<RegisteredAgent> at
construction, so it is complete before any compile can run and the trap
is structurally impossible. Deleted along the way:

- the AUTO_EXPOSE_AS_TOOL_METADATA_KEY wire protocol (stamping in the
  registrar, parsing in the merger, the re-export on AgentCompiler)
- the volatile cache + double-checked locking + failure-retry logic
- AgentCompiler's MetadataDAO constructor and mergeAutoExposedTools delegate

The registrar still persists each WorkflowDef — that's needed for
SUB_WORKFLOW dispatch by name — but it's now a dumb compile-and-persist
loop. A blank autoExpose tool name now fails fast at boot instead of
being silently skipped.

Tests rewritten to the bean-list model; the obsolete cache-behavior
tests are replaced by construction-time pins. Validated per CLAUDE.md by
mutating merge() into a no-op: exactly the injection-asserting tests
failed, guards stayed green.

test(e2e): add Python media-input suite (image → vision model)

Adds Suite 25, the inverse of Suite 7 (media generation): it passes an
image as INPUT via runtime.run(..., media=[...]) and verifies a
vision-capable model actually receives and reads it.

Deterministic, non-LLM-judged: the image renders a distinctive,
unguessable token (MELON7391); the agent transcribes it and we assert
the exact token appears in the output. A counterfactual case runs the
same prompt with NO media and asserts the token is absent, proving the
positive case is real (the token only appears if the image was seen).

Parametrized across OpenAI and Anthropic. The Anthropic positive case is
skipped: the server forwards media to OpenAI but does not attach it to
the Anthropic provider request, so the model receives no image. The
Anthropic counterfactual still runs and passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(e2e): make Suite 25 media image self-contained

Address review: don't depend on a public image host (dummyimage.com) at
run time. Embed the PNG as base64 in the test and load it from the local
filesystem — write the bytes to the server's allowed media directory and
pass that path as media. No external host, no HTTP server.

The dir defaults to ~/worker-payload/ (the server's allowed dir when
conductor.file-storage.parentDir is unset — the default `agentspan server
start` config) and can be overridden with AGENTSPAN_MEDIA_DIR for
deployments with a custom allowed dir. Assumes server + test share a host
(the standard local/bundle e2e setup). A comment documents how to
regenerate the embedded image from a public endpoint.
